lines.trans: One bite... Javier, close your eyes! That tastes exactly like Grandfather's cake!
Rocio baked it this morning when Madam Carmen told her our Friday story.
What kind of magical guesthouse did you stumble into, little brother?
The kind that fixes attic lamps in the rain and guards a stranger's bag.
Then tell me why the poor gentleman behind the front desk looks ready to cry.
Oh! Did you see Ernesto through the window? I tried to smile doubly wide!
Rocio, is something wrong inside? Did the boiler break again?
Worse than a pipe... a registered letter came from the building owner at noon.
A property letter? Let Javier and me see it—I work in municipal contracts, and he knows heritage law!
Wait, Tomas—you still work at City Hall's contract desk?!
Both of you?! Leave your teacups—come inside this very second!

cerrar.gloss: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)

meanings.en: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: cierro).

meanings.note: Plural los ojos.

examples.trans: We see the eyes from the door.

saber.gloss: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.en: to know (a fact / how to); to taste (saber a)

meanings.note: Formed from exacta + -mente.

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.

The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuento).

examples.text: Conté doce tazas en el armario.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

arreglar.gloss: to fix; to repair; to tidy

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

examples.trans: We see the dots from the door.

examples.text: Casi lloro de risa con tu historia.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Followed directly by an infinitive (intenté sonreír).

meanings.note: Conjugates like reír (sonrío, sonrió); imperative plural: ¡sonreíd!.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.

meanings.en: to return; to come back; to do again (volver a + inf)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: vuelvo), past participle vuelto; volverse + adj = become.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: llegué.

meanings.note: Feminine: la dueña.

meanings.note: Multi-storey town building.

examples.text: Vemos los edificios desde la puerta.

meanings.note: Registro de la propiedad = Land/Property Registry.

examples.trans: The property is here.

examples.text: Vemos las propiedades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the properties from the door.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Accented pronoun after para, por, a, de, sin (distinct from possessive mi).

examples.text: Vemos los contratos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the contracts from the door.

meanings.note: Plural municipales.

examples.trans: It is a municipal piece.

examples.trans: Smart thinking, Clara. Javier reads city building rules every single week.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

seguir.gloss: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)

meanings.en: to continue; to keep (doing); to go straight (seguir recto)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sigo, sigue, siguió); seguir + gerund = keep doing.

examples.trans: The office is here.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.

See you later, have a good day!
